question.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are arithmetic sequences?

I. $65,\,55,\,44,\,33,\,…$

II. $340,\,430,\,520,\,610,\,…$

III. $9,\,19,\,199,\,1\,999,\,…$
question.worked_solution:
To determine whether each sequence is an arithmetic sequence, we need to look at the jumps between terms in the sequence. If the jumps are the same, then they indeed represent a common difference of an arithmetic sequence.

- In sequence I, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence I is not an arithmetic sequence.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/dbd0f6dbb2c752dc887e3b9b2495d4e28facf9a01b03c24523f62788babe9ca1.png)

- In sequence II, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence II is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=90.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/d7abd51d29e0e8707d42842a0927deef78c6e617925c8f32cb33c77be164e68e.png)

- In sequence III, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence III is not an arithmetic sequence.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/e56729dca74eaa7667b845dead4f02e5667e3575b4d567bd344e6ee1b926812e.png)

In conclusion, only sequence II is an arithmetic sequence.
